title: Multi-step finding where no individual function is vulnerable in isolation
scenario: Three functions are each correct on their own. Composed in one transaction, a stale cached rate, a permissionless cache refresh and a rebate claim let an attacker claim a rebate computed at a rate that no longer applies.
exercises: a composition finding is judged on the composed path, not function by function
a long attack path is not a reason to reject

mutations.name: individual correctness does not refute the composed path
mutations.expect_error: technical_claim is UNSUPPORTED but no decisive or strong counterexample with evidence targets it

mutations.name: a long path is only supported while every link holds
mutations.expect_error: adjudication.attack_path is SUPPORTED but step 5 is UNKNOWN

challenged_finding.claimed_impact: Rebate inflation by composing a cache refresh with a rebate claim

prosecutor.strongest_claim: Refreshing the rate cache between accrual and claim lets the attacker claim at an outdated favorable rate within one transaction.

attacker_capability.statement: Any address can call refreshCache() and claim().

required_state.statement: An accrued rebate exists and the cached rate differs from the live rate.

execution_path.statement: accrue() stamps the entitlement, refreshCache() rewrites the rate, and claim() recomputes the payout from the new cache.

evidence.ref: forge test -m testComposedRebateInflation: payout 7.2 percent above entitlement

violated_property.statement: A rebate pays at the rate in force when it accrued.

evidence.ref: contracts/Rebate.sol:132 recomputes rather than reading the stamped rate

impact.statement: The attacker extracts the difference from the rebate pool on every claim.

defender.strongest_counterargument: Each function is individually correct and independently audited, so there may be no defect to report.

evidence.ref: audit report 2026-01, findings 4.1 to 4.9 cover each function separately

challenges.statement: Each function is correct in isolation and was audited as such.
The rate divergence may be too small or too short-lived to exploit profitably.

evidence.ref: observed divergence window 14 blocks at block 21288401

challenges.statement: refreshCache() may be keeper-restricted in production.
Atomic composition may be prevented by a per-transaction guard.
The rebate pool may absorb the difference without user loss.

challenge_matrix.finding: Both entry points are permissionless and composable in a single transaction.
The rate divergence occurs on every oracle update and lasts until the next refresh.
No reentrancy guard or keeper restriction applies to either call.
The composed state is reached with ordinary calls in one transaction.
The executed test shows a 7.2 percent overpayment drawn from the rebate pool.

assumptions.statement: refreshCache() and claim() can be called in one transaction by the same address.
claim() recomputes from the cache rather than the stamped rate.
A favorable divergence is available often enough to matter.

attack_path.transition: Attacker accrues a rebate entitlement at the current rate.
Attacker waits for the live rate to move away from the cached rate.
In one transaction, attacker calls refreshCache().
cachedRate is rewritten to the favorable value.
Attacker calls claim() in the same transaction.
Payout is recomputed from the new cache and overpays by 7.2 percent.

counterexamples.reason: Each function is individually correct, so a per-function review finds nothing; the defect exists only in the composition.

decisive_facts.fact: claim() recomputes the payout from the mutable cache rather than the rate stamped at accrual.
Both entry points are permissionless and composable atomically.

severity_challenge.demonstrated_impact: 7.2 percent overpayment per claim drawn from the rebate pool
severity_challenge.attacker_requirements: None beyond gas and the ability to observe a rate divergence.
severity_challenge.policy_alignment: Matches the program's theft of protocol funds tier for smart contracts.

adjudication.strongest_supporting_evidence: claim() recomputes from a cache the attacker can rewrite in the same transaction.
adjudication.strongest_opposing_evidence: Each function is individually correct and was audited as such.
adjudication.rationale: Function-by-function correctness does not answer the composed question. The composed path is permissionless, atomic, and executed; the finding stands.
